reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports using short AIMD with a Gaussian approximation to extract vibrational entropy for elemental solids and mentions a HEA example, but it explicitly warns that the Gaussian approximation may fail when correlations beyond it are needed and that the method is most useful when simulations are already done for other purposes. It does not provide evidence that an ML surrogate trained on such data can accurately reproduce full free-energy landscapes or that order-of-magnitude speedups are achievable for multicomponent systems.
premises: Short AIMD can capture vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron-vibration coupling via covariance matrices
A Gaussian approximation for atomic displacements is valid for the target systems
An ML potential trained on short AIMD data can faithfully reproduce the free-energy landscape
The method works for multicomponent high-entropy alloys, not just elemental solids
The hybrid method achieves order-of-magnitude speedup over explicit AIMD/TOR-TILD for HEAs
